content.text: The Plex DB is in a docker volume and the container ships its own SQLite binary. I'll copy the DB and query the music section for albums with artist and genre tags.

input.command:
ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'docker exec plex sh -c "
cp \"/config/Library/Application Support/Plex Media Server/Plug-in Support/Databases/com.plexapp.plugins.library.db\" /tmp/lib.db 2>/dev/null
cp \"/config/Library/Application Support/Plex Media Server/Plug-in Support/Databases/com.plexapp.plugins.library.db-wal\" /tmp/lib.db-wal 2>/dev/null
S=\"/usr/lib/plexmediaserver/Plex SQLite\"
echo SECTIONS; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select id,name,section_type from library_sections;\"
echo COUNTS; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select library_section_id, metadata_type, count(*) from metadata_items group by 1,2;\"
"'
input.description: Copy Plex DB and list library sections

content.text: 647 albums across 281 artists. Now I'll dump every album with its artist, year and genre tags into a local file so I can analyse the collection.

input.command:
mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/e41a0627-f401-4e2b-9377-d700dde4d583/scratchpad && ssh -o BatchMode=yes mm@docker-host 'docker exec plex sh -c "
S=\"/usr/lib/plexmediaserver/Plex SQLite\"
\"\$S\" -separator \"	\" /tmp/lib.db \"
select ar.title as artist, al.title as album, al.year,
  (select group_concat(t.tag, \\\";\\\") from taggings tg join tags t on t.id=tg.tag_id where tg.metadata_item_id=al.id and t.tag_type=1) as album_genres,
  (select group_concat(t.tag, \\\";\\\") from taggings tg join tags t on t.id=tg.tag_id where tg.metadata_item_id=ar.id and t.tag_type=1) as artist_genres
from metadata_items al join metadata_items ar on ar.id=al.parent_id
where al.metadata_type=9 and al.library_section_id=3
order by ar.title_sort, al.year;\"
"' > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/e41a0627-f401-4e2b-9377-d700dde4d583/scratchpad/albums.tsv; wc -l /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/e41a0627-f401-4e2b-9377-d700dde4d583/scratchpad/albums.tsv; head -5 /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/e41a0627-f401-4e2b-9377-d700dde4d583/scratchpad/albums.tsv

content.text:
Your Plex music library holds 647 albums, and roughly 400 of them are hip hop. The profile is clear: 90s East Coast canon, conscious and backpacker rap, the Def Jux and Rhymesayers lineage, the Backwoodz and Griselda underground, Alchemist and Madlib production, TDE and Dreamville, plus a solid UK strand. The list below fills the gaps in those lanes, prioritising albums where you already own the artist or a direct sequel but not the acclaimed original.

**Golden-era canon you're missing**

1. JAY-Z – Reasonable Doubt (1996). You have six Jay albums but not his debut.
2. Ghostface Killah – Supreme Clientele (2000). You own Supreme Clientele 2 but not the original.
3. Wu-Tang Clan – Wu-Tang Forever (1997). Only 36 Chambers is in the library.
4. Raekwon – Only Built 4 Cuban Linx… Pt. II (2009). Widely rated the best Wu sequel.
5. Big L – Lifestylez ov da Poor & Dangerous (1995). You have his posthumous work but not the debut.
6. Mobb Deep – Hell on Earth (1996). The follow-up to The Infamous.
7. Gang Starr – Hard to Earn (1994). Only Moment of Truth is present.
8. Pete Rock & C.L. Smooth – The Main Ingredient (1994). Pairs with Mecca and the Soul Brother.
9. Eric B. & Rakim – Follow the Leader (1988).
10. Public Enemy – Fear of a Black Planet (1990).
11. Redman – Muddy Waters (1996). You own Muddy Waters Too but not the first.
12. De La Soul – Buhloone Mindstate (1993). The one gap in your De La run.
13. Fugees – The Score (1996). You have Miseducation but not this.
14. Dr. Dre – 2001 (1999).
15. Common – One Day It'll All Make Sense (1997). The missing link between Resurrection and Like Water.
16. A Tribe Called Quest – We Got It from Here… Thank You 4 Your Service (2016).

**Left-field and underground, matching your Def Jux, Stones Throw and Backwoodz shelves**

17. Dr. Octagon – Dr. Octagonecologyst (1996). You have Kool Keith and Ultramagnetic MC's already.
18. Cannibal Ox – The Cold Vein (2001). El-P produced, sits next to Funcrusher Plus.
19. Aesop Rock – Labor Days (2001). His most acclaimed record, and the one before Bazooka Tooth.
20. Open Mike Eagle – Brick Body Kids Still Daydream (2017). His peak, and you own three later albums.
21. billy woods & Kenny Segal – Hiding Places (2019). Frequently cited as his best.
22. Ka – Honor Killed the Samurai (2016).
23. Roc Marciano – Marcberg (2010). The album that started the whole Griselda-adjacent sound you collect.
24. Westside Gunn – Pray for Paris (2020). You have Benny, Conway and Boldy but no Westside Gunn.
25. Boldy James & The Alchemist – The Price of Tea in China (2020).
26. Danny Brown – Atrocity Exhibition (2016). You only have his two most recent.
27. JPEGMAFIA – Veteran (2018). Fits with clipping., Injury Reserve and Dälek.

**Modern acclaimed gaps**

28. Pusha T – Daytona (2018). You have It's Almost Dry.
29. Big Boi – Sir Lucious Left Foot: The Son of Chico Dusty (2010). Completes the OutKast shelf.
30. Rapsody – Laila's Wisdom (2017). You have her 2024 and 2026 albums only.

Near misses worth a second tier if you want more: Stormzy's Gang Signs & Prayer, Roots Manuva's Run Come Save Me and Kano's Made in the Manor for the UK side. Madlib's Shades of Blue and Jaylib's Champion Sound for the Stones Throw side. Navy Blue's Ways of Knowing and R.A.P. Ferreira's Purple Moonlight Pages for the MIKE and woods lane. Mac Miller's Faces, Kid Cudi's Man on the Moon, Drake's Take Care and Lil Wayne's Tha Carter III for the mainstream gaps.

One housekeeping note: 151 albums have no genre tag in Plex, including the Alchemist, Boldy James and Roc Marciano entries. A metadata refresh on the Music section would fix your genre filters.

echo SECTION; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select id,name,agent,scanner,language from library_sections where id=3;\"

echo GUID_PREFIX_ALBUMS; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select substr(guid,1,instr(guid,\\\"://\\\")+2), count(*) from metadata_items where library_section_id=3 and metadata_type=9 group by 1;\"
echo GUID_PREFIX_ARTISTS; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select substr(guid,1,instr(guid,\\\"://\\\")+2), count(*) from metadata_items where library_section_id=3 and metadata_type=8 group by 1;\"
echo UNTAGGED_BY_GUID; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select substr(al.guid,1,8), count(*) from metadata_items al where al.metadata_type=9 and al.library_section_id=3 and not exists (select 1 from taggings tg join tags t on t.id=tg.tag_id where tg.metadata_item_id=al.id and t.tag_type=1) group by 1;\"
echo NO_YEAR; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select count(*) from metadata_items where library_section_id=3 and metadata_type=9 and (year is null or year=0);\"

echo VARIOUS; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select title, id from metadata_items where library_section_id=3 and metadata_type=8 and (title like \\\"%Various%\\\" or title like \\\"%Unknown%\\\" or title=\\\"\\\");\"
echo ARTIST_NO_GENRE; \"\$S\" /tmp/lib.db \"select count(*) from metadata_items ar where ar.metadata_type=8 and ar.library_section_id=3 and not exists (select 1 from taggings tg join tags t on t.id=tg.tag_id where tg.metadata_item_id=ar.id and t.tag_type=1);\"

import csv,collections,os,re

    d=os.path.dirname(r[0]); tags.setdefault(d,[]).append(r)

        n+=1
        if not r[1]: miss['artist']+=1
        if not r[2]: miss['albumartist']+=1
        if not r[3]: miss['album']+=1
        if not r[4]: miss['date']+=1

# map untagged plex albums -> folder genre
def plexgenre(g):
    g=g.lower()
    if re.search(r'hip.?hop|rap|grime|drill|trap|boom bap|g-funk',g): return 'Rap'
    if re.search(r'r&b|soul|neo.?soul|funk',g): return 'R&B'

    if re.search(r'pop|rock|indie|alternative|metal|punk|singer',g): return 'Pop/Rock'
    if 'country' in g: return 'Country'
    if 'folk' in g: return 'Folk'
    if 'reggae' in g: return 'Reggae'
    if 'k-pop' in g or 'kpop' in g: return 'Pop/Rock'
    return None

    d=os.path.dirname(f.replace('/data/music/',''))
    rows=tags.get(d,[])

    raw=gs.most_common(1)[0][0] if gs else ''
    pg=plexgenre(raw) if raw else ''
    out.write('\t'.join([aid,artist,album,year,raw,pg or ''])+'\n')

content.text:
All changes are applied and verified. Here is the full picture.

## Plex metadata: fixed

Every album and artist in the Music section now carries a genre, and the field is locked so future agent refreshes won't blank it again.

| Item | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Albums with no genre | 151 | 0 |
| Artists with no genre | 24 | 1 (Various Artists, intentionally left) |
| Unmatched albums | 1 | 0 |
| Albums with no artwork | 5 | 0 |

- **Genre source.** Where the files carried an embedded genre tag I mapped it into Plex's existing vocabulary (Rap, R&B, Jazz, Pop/Rock). For the 57 albums with no embedded tag I assigned it by hand. Everything landed as Rap except AUDREY NUNA, BLK ODYSSY, Sol ChYld and Sasha Keable (R&B), Kiefer and Makaya McCraven's Off the Record (Jazz), and André 3000's piano sketches (Pop/Rock, from its tag).
- **Chance the Rapper, Star Line** was the only unmatched album. It's now matched to MusicBrainz with year and release date locked to 2025.
- **Artwork.** Four albums had no art anywhere: not in Plex, not in the folder, not embedded. I pulled front covers from the Cover Art Archive for Larry June's Doing It for Me, Babyface Ray's Summer's Mine, Bashy's Being Poor Is Expensive and Bruiser Wolf's POTLUCK. Kota the Friend's Once In A Blue Moon resolved itself on refresh.

## Files on disk: Plex is finding everything

All 9,581 audio files under /mnt/music (9,466 FLAC, 115 MP3) are indexed. Nothing is missing in either direction. Permissions are consistent (media:media). I cleaned the safe junk:

- Removed 19 .DS_Store files.
- Removed a 512 KB half-written temp file left in The Alchemist Sandwich (the real track exists alongside it).
- Removed 56 empty directories, mostly Lidarr leftovers from artist renames (Kanye West to Ye, Mos Def to Yasiin Bey, and six case-only duplicates like Billy Woods vs billy woods). Artist folders dropped from 292 to 285 with zero audio touched.

**Duplicates I did not delete** because they contain real audio. Your call on each:

1. **Kendrick Lamar, The Steppers Tour.** Two identical 5-track copies (121 MB each). The Amazon Originals folder is the manual import. The Lidarr-named folder is canonical. Plex shows the album twice.
2. **A Minecraft Movie 16** at the library root holds tracks 22 to 25 only. The full 25-track album sits correctly under Mark Mothersbaugh. Delete the root folder.
3. **KPop Demon Hunters** is split across three folders and three Plex entries. The Lidarr-named folder under KPop Demon Hunters Cast is the most complete (12 tracks), but its file 01 is tagged as track 6 so the album shows Takedown twice and lacks track 1. Fix that one tag, then remove the scene-named folder (11 tracks) and the 2-track Various Artists folder.

**Lower priority observations.** 51 album folders still have scene-release names with brackets and catalogue numbers rather than Lidarr's clean format. Lidarr has "rename tracks" on but "delete empty folders" off, which is why leftovers accumulate. Lidarr also reports the MyAnonamouse indexer failing for over 6 hours. Embedded tags are patchy (1,683 files lack a genre, 3,306 lack embedded art) but that has no effect while Plex's "Prefer local metadata" stays off, which is the right setting for this library.

Comment on: "1. **Kendrick Lamar, The Steppers Tour.** Two identical 5-track copies (121 MB each). The Amazon Originals folder is the manual import. The Lidarr-named folder is canonical. Plex shows the album twice. 2. **A Minecraft Movie 16** at the library root holds tracks 22 to 25 only. The full 25-track album sits correctly under Mark Mothersbaugh. Delete the root folder. 3. **KPop Demon Hunters** is split across three folders and three Plex entries. The Lidarr-named folder under KPop Demon Hunters Cast is the most complete (12 tracks), but its file 01 is tagged as track 6 so the album shows Takedown twice and lacks track 1. Fix that one tag, then remove the scene-named folder (11 tracks) and the 2-track Various Artists folder."
> cleanup all duplicates

## Annotation 2 (line 32)
Comment on: "**Lower priority observations.** 51 album folders still have scene-release names with brackets and catalogue numbers rather than Lidarr's clean format. Lidarr has "rename tracks" on but "delete empty folders" off, which is why leftovers accumulate. Lidarr also reports the MyAnonamouse indexer failing for over 6 hours. Embedded tags are patchy (1,683 files lack a genre, 3,306 lack embedded art) but that has no effect while Plex's "Prefer local metadata" stays off, which is the right setting for this library."
> cleanup naming, set delete empty folders on, resolve patchy tags

Comment on: "Lidarr manages this library with 289 artists, so these can be added there for automatic acquisition. I haven't queued them since that triggers downloads. Say the word and I'll add all 42 to Lidarr as monitored albums."

content.text:
All requested work is done or running to completion on its own. Here is where things stand.

## Duplicates: all cleaned

- **KPop Demon Hunters** is now one 12-track album in Plex. The byte-identical duplicate of track 6 that was masquerading as track 1 was replaced with the real track 1 from the Various Artists folder. The scene-named folder and the Various Artists folder are gone. The two Plex entries were merged and track 1 renumbered and locked.
- **Kendrick Lamar, The Steppers Tour.** The Amazon Originals copy was removed. One entry remains.
- **A Minecraft Movie 16** root folder removed. The full album under Mark Mothersbaugh is intact.
- **Freddie Gibbs, You Only Die 1nce.** A second encode of track 8 in a stray "(2024)" folder was doubling the track in Plex. Removed.

## Naming, empty folders, tags

- **54 leftover folders deleted.** The scene-named folders contained no audio, only cue, log, playlist and cover files left behind after Lidarr had already moved the tracks into clean folders. Removing them also emptied the case-duplicate artist folders (Billy Woods, Kanye West, Kaytranada). The library is now 279 artist folders with no non-audio files except embedded-adjacent cover images.
- **Lidarr renamed 348 files** across 17 artists that had drifted from its format (curly apostrophes, casing, "Ms. Lauryn Hill").
- **Lidarr config changed:** delete empty folders is on, and "write audio tags" is set to all files with cover art embedding, so future imports get full tags.
- **Full retag pass is running.** Lidarr is rewriting tags on all 9,648 tracked files from MusicBrainz, which fixes the missing genre, album artist and embedded art. It is slow and will take a few hours. A background job on docker-host waits for it, retags the KPop folder once more, then triggers a Plex scan. Log is at `/tmp/wait_retag.log` on docker-host.

## Albums requested via Lidarr: 42 of 42

All 42 are monitored and searched. Lidarr's metadata proxy was returning 503s, so four were resolved through Lidarr's own album list and artist lookup instead. Progress at the time of writing:

| State | Count |
|---|---|
| Imported and visible in Plex | 28 |
| Downloaded, import pending | 9 |
| Still downloading | 5 |

Every newly imported album has a genre in Plex. Three that Plex left blank (Hiding Places, Ways of Knowing, Gang Signs & Prayer) were set to Rap and locked. Mac Miller's Faces is a mixtape, which your Lidarr metadata profile excludes, so a future artist refresh may drop it. If it disappears, re-add it manually.

## Multi-disc and split-album check

I compared every track's disc and track number in Plex against the file names and tags. All 31 multi-disc albums are intact with no missing discs. No folder is split across Plex albums any more. Two classes of cosmetic edition mismatch exist, neither loses tracks:

- **Disc 2 folded into disc 1** on five albums (Sabrina Carpenter, Chappell Roan, Billie Eilish, Pantera's Vulgar Display of Power, Blood Orange). Lidarr chose a two-disc deluxe release; Plex matched the single-disc edition and numbered the bonus tracks sequentially. All tracks present.
- **Gaps from a bigger Plex edition.** Don Toliver's Love Sick, Apollo Brown's Sardines, Stress Eater's Everybody Eats and Alicia Keys' Songs in A Minor are complete per Lidarr's release but Plex matched a deluxe edition, so a few slots show empty. Plex can only match at release-group level, so this is not fixable from the Plex side.

One genuine gap: **Drake's For All the Dogs** is missing tracks 4 and 6, Fear of Heights and First Person Shooter. The folder has 21 of 23 tracks and Lidarr believes the album is complete, so it will not re-grab. Deleting the album in Lidarr and re-searching would fetch a full copy.

## Lidarr can't match these folders

44 files sit in folders Lidarr won't track, so the retag pass skips them: Czarface Meets Ghostface (12), Mach-Hommy's Pray for Haiti (16), Smino's Maybe in Nirvana (10), Mark Mothersbaugh's Minecraft tracks 22 to 25 (4), plus one KPop file that the refresh should pick up. They play fine in Plex. Matching them in Lidarr's manual import would let it tag them too.

Lidarr's MyAnonamouse indexer is still failing health checks, which limits search coverage for the remaining downloads.

Both requests are complete.

## Drake, For All the Dogs: regrabbed in full

Lidarr deleted the 21 partial files, I switched the monitored release to the explicit edition, and the search grabbed a FLAC Scary Hours Edition from Redacted within seconds. It imported as 29 tracks across two discs. Plex now shows the album as "For All The Dogs Scary Hours Edition" with a clean 1-01 through 1-23 and 2-01 through 2-06. Fear of Heights and First Person Shooter are in place.

## Untracked folders: all matched in Lidarr

| Folder | Result |
|---|---|
| Czarface Meets Ghostface (12) | Imported as the Instrumentals release |
| Mach-Hommy, Pray for Haiti (16) | Imported |
| Smino, Maybe in Nirvana (10) | Imported |
| Minecraft soundtrack (25) | Lidarr switched to the 25-track release, all tracked |
| KPop track 1 | Imported |

One note on Czarface. The files are tagged as the vocal album, but both Lidarr and Plex fingerprint them as the instrumental edition, so I imported them under that. If you believe they're the vocal version, listen to one and I'll remap it.

Lidarr now tracks 10,315 files, the same as the count on disk. Nothing is untracked. Plex holds 684 albums and 10,307 tracks with no split folders, no albums merged from multiple folders, no disc or track collisions, and no duplicate artist-and-title pairs. Every album has a genre.

## Still running

The library-wide retag pass is about a quarter done and will run for an hour or two more. The background waiter on docker-host triggers a Plex rescan when it finishes.
